title: Are you a workaholic or just a hard worker? With Malissa Clark, PhD

sentences.en: It's five o'clock and your workday is technically over, but you tell yourself you'll just answer one more email.
sentences.zh: 现在是下午五点，按理说你的工作时间已经结束了，但你告诉自己，只要再回一封邮件就好。

sentences.en: Before you know it, two hours have passed and you're still at your desk.
sentences.zh: 不知不觉中，两小时过去了，你依然坐在办公桌前。

sentences.en: Or you're supposed to be on vacation, but you can't resist reading work emails and responding every time your phone pings with a message from a colleague.
sentences.zh: 又或者你本该在休假，却总是忍不住查看工作邮件，每当手机响起同事发来的消息，你都会忍不住回复。

sentences.en: In our always connected world, it's easier than ever to let work encroach on every hour of the day.
sentences.zh: 在这个时刻保持在线的世界里，工作比以往任何时候都更容易侵占我们每一天的每一小时。

sentences.en: But psychologists who study workaholism say that compulsive overwork is detrimental to our physical and mental health and perhaps surprisingly, even to our careers.
sentences.zh: 但研究工作狂现象的心理学家表示，强迫性的过度工作对我们的身心健康有害，而且令人惊讶的是，甚至对我们的职业生涯也有害。

sentences.en: Today, we're going to talk to a psychologist who studies workaholism about what it is and how to combat it.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们将与一位研究工作狂现象的心理学家探讨什么是工作狂，以及如何应对它。

sentences.en: What's the difference between being a workaholic and just being a hard worker who's invested in her job?
sentences.zh: 工作狂与仅仅是投入工作的勤奋员工之间有什么区别？

sentences.en: Is workaholism an addiction?
sentences.zh: 工作狂是一种成瘾吗？

sentences.en: How does it affect people's physical and mental health and their relationships?
sentences.zh: 它如何影响人们的身心健康和人际关系？

sentences.en: What can you do if you recognize workaholic tendencies in yourself or in someone you care about?
sentences.zh: 如果你发现自己或你在意的人有工作狂倾向，该怎么办？

sentences.en: And what can organizations and employers do to encourage a healthy relationship with work among their employees?
sentences.zh: 组织和雇主又能做些什么来鼓励员工与工作建立健康的关系？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学谈话》，这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: My guest today is Dr. Melissa Clark, a professor of industrial organizational psychology at the University of Georgia, where she directs the Healthy Work Lab.
sentences.zh: 我今天的嘉宾是佐治亚大学工业与组织心理学教授梅丽莎·克拉克博士，她在那里负责健康工作实验室。

sentences.en: She's a leading expert on workaholism, overwork, and employee well-being.
sentences.zh: 她是工作狂、过度工作和员工福祉方面的顶尖专家。

sentences.en: Her research has been published in top academic journals and featured in publications including Time, The New York Times, The Atlantic, and U.S.
sentences.zh: 她的研究发表在顶级学术期刊上，并被《时代》周刊、《纽约时报》、《大西洋》月刊以及《美国新闻与世界报道》等刊物报道。

sentences.en: News and World Report.
sentences.zh: 新闻与世界报道。

sentences.en: Her 2024 book, Never Not Working, Why the Always-On Culture is Bad for Business and How to Fix It, was recognized as a top management book by People Management, Management Today,
sentences.zh: 她2024年的著作《永不停止工作：为什么“时刻在线”的文化对商业有害以及如何修复它》被《人事管理》、《今日管理》评为顶级管理书籍，

sentences.en: and The Next Big Idea Club.
sentences.zh: 以及“下一个大创意俱乐部”评选为顶级管理书籍。

sentences.en: She also recently spoke with APA's magazine, Monitor on Psychology, for an article on workaholism and work addiction.
sentences.zh: 她最近还接受了美国心理学会杂志《心理学监测》的采访，讨论了关于工作狂和工作成瘾的文章。

sentences.en: Dr. Clark, thank you for joining me.
sentences.zh: 克拉克博士，感谢您参加我的节目。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for having me.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我。

sentences.en: I've seen workaholism go by a few different names, including work addiction and compulsive overwork.
sentences.zh: 我见过工作狂有几种不同的称呼，包括工作成瘾和强迫性过度工作。

sentences.en: What term do you use in your research, and how is this situation different from just working really hard or being very dedicated to one's job?
sentences.zh: 在您的研究中，您使用什么术语？这种情况与仅仅是努力工作或对工作非常敬业有什么不同？

sentences.en: I use the term workaholism.
sentences.zh: 我使用“工作狂”这个术语。

sentences.en: To be honest, I don't love the term work addiction, but it is what it is at this point.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我不喜欢“工作成瘾”这个词，但目前大家就是这么叫的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's what is coined.
sentences.zh: 这就是大家通用的说法。

sentences.en: It's not a formal addiction in the DSM, and I'm also not a clinical psychologist, which is partly why I don't use the work addiction term specifically.
sentences.zh: 它在《精神疾病诊断与统计手册》（DSM）中并不是一种正式的成瘾症，而且我本人也不是临床心理学家，这在一定程度上是我不专门使用“工作成瘾”这个词的原因。

sentences.en: But workaholism is multifaceted, and a lot of people don't realize that.
sentences.zh: 但工作狂现象是多方面的，很多人并没有意识到这一点。

sentences.en: They think, OK, it's just someone who works all the time.
sentences.zh: 他们认为，好吧，这只是指那些一直工作的人。

sentences.en: But those examples that you pointed out really touch on how nuanced it is.
sentences.zh: 但你指出的那些例子确实触及了它有多么微妙。

sentences.en: And the way I study it and measure it is actually with four different components.
sentences.zh: 我研究和衡量它的方式实际上包含四个不同的组成部分。

sentences.en: There's a motivational piece where people feel like they ought to be working all the time.
sentences.zh: 首先是动机层面，人们觉得他们应该一直工作。

sentences.en: You probably have heard of a concept called intrinsic motivation, which is working because you love to work.
sentences.zh: 你可能听说过“内在动机”这个概念，即因为热爱工作而工作。

sentences.en: Workaholism is driven by introjected motivation.
sentences.zh: 而工作狂则是由“内摄动机”驱动的。

sentences.en: It's a concept that psychologists know.
sentences.zh: 这是心理学家熟知的一个概念。

sentences.en: It's working because you feel like you ought to.
sentences.zh: 它是指因为你觉得“应该”做而工作。

sentences.en: It's partially internalized values of society and, you know, things that you learn growing up.
sentences.zh: 这部分源于社会内化的价值观，以及你在成长过程中学到的东西。

sentences.en: But it's not truly of your own volition.
sentences.zh: 但这并非真正出于你自己的意愿。

sentences.en: So it's this kind of controlled motivation.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一种受控的动机。

sentences.en: But I just describe it as pit in my stomach, you know, feeling like I ought to be working.
sentences.zh: 我把它描述为胃里有一种揪心的感觉，你知道，就是觉得我应该在工作。

sentences.en: The second component is the cognitive component where you're thinking about work all the time.
sentences.zh: 第二个组成部分是认知层面，即你一直在思考工作。

sentences.en: And this is often not talked about enough, in my opinion, because it's this like running dialogue about work in your head.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，这一点往往讨论得不够，因为它就像你脑子里一直在进行关于工作的对话。

sentences.en: It keeps you up, keeps you from falling asleep.
sentences.zh: 它让你彻夜难眠，无法入睡。

sentences.en: It distracts you when you're talking with your family.
sentences.zh: 当你和家人交谈时，它会让你分心。

sentences.en: And what are you doing?
sentences.zh: 你在做什么？

sentences.en: You're thinking about work.
sentences.zh: 你在想工作。

sentences.en: So that's the cognitive component.
sentences.zh: 这就是认知组成部分。

sentences.en: There's an emotional piece to it that goes along with introjected motivation, this feeling of guilt and anxiety that kind of builds and builds if you're not working,
sentences.zh: 它还有一个与内摄动机相伴的情感层面，即如果你不工作，那种负罪感和焦虑感就会不断累积，

sentences.en: which is partly what kind of drives you to pick up the phone or check your email.
sentences.zh: 这在一定程度上驱使你去拿起手机或查看邮件。

sentences.en: And then the fourth component is the most obvious.
sentences.zh: 第四个组成部分是最明显的。

sentences.en: It's the behavioral component.
sentences.zh: 即行为层面。

sentences.en: And workaholics do tend to work longer than expected, longer than their colleagues.
sentences.zh: 工作狂确实倾向于比预期工作更长的时间，比同事工作的时间更长。

sentences.en: It is related to work hours, but it's honestly just kind of a moderate relationship or correlation.
sentences.zh: 它与工作时长有关，但老实说，这只是一种中等程度的关系或相关性。

sentences.en: So doing things like working on vacation, all of that is part of the behavioral component.
sentences.zh: 所以，像在度假时工作之类的行为，都是行为组成部分的一部分。

sentences.en: So it is truly multifaceted.
sentences.zh: 所以它确实是多方面的。

sentences.en: You can think about it sort of like a compulsion to work using that loosely and not like in the technical clinical psychology sense.
sentences.zh: 你可以把它想象成一种工作强迫症，这里是泛指，而不是从技术性的临床心理学意义上来说。

sentences.en: Now, you've studied how workaholism affects people's lives, their physical health, their mental health, and their relationships.
sentences.zh: 现在，您研究了工作狂如何影响人们的生活、身体健康、心理健康以及人际关系。

sentences.en: What have you and other researchers in this area found?
sentences.zh: 您和其他该领域的研究人员发现了什么？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So pretty universally negative outcomes for individuals, for those around them, family, both in terms of physical health outcomes.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，对于个人及其周围的人（如家庭成员）来说，结果几乎普遍是负面的，无论是在身体健康结果方面。

sentences.en: We find that workaholism is linked to poor health.
sentences.zh: 我们发现工作狂与健康状况不佳有关。

sentences.en: You know, they tend to not exercise as much sometimes or sleep very well.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们有时往往不怎么锻炼，或者睡眠质量不好。

sentences.en: And that kind of takes a toll.
sentences.zh: 这会造成一定的损害。

sentences.en: But there's some recent research showing links with cardiovascular risk and actigraph studies, like showing the sleep impacts of workaholism and even linked to inflammation.
sentences.zh: 但最近有一些研究显示，工作狂与心血管风险有关，通过活动记录仪研究显示了工作狂对睡眠的影响，甚至与炎症有关。

sentences.en: And so we see these health impacts.
sentences.zh: 所以我们看到了这些健康影响。

sentences.en: We see self-reported lower, you know, mental health, greater burnout, just generally, you know,
sentences.zh: 我们看到自我报告的心理健康水平较低，倦怠感更强，总的来说，你知道，

sentences.en: kind of self-report of how you're feeling tends to be universally negative and impacts on the family.
sentences.zh: 对自己感觉的自我报告往往普遍是负面的，并且会对家庭产生影响。

sentences.en: I personally conducted interviews of spouses of workaholics, and we really see the impacts of the family by talking to the spouses.
sentences.zh: 我亲自采访过工作狂的配偶，通过与他们交谈，我们确实看到了工作狂对家庭的影响。

sentences.en: You know, the relationship quality suffers.
sentences.zh: 你知道，关系质量会受损。

sentences.en: The spouse is taking more on.
sentences.zh: 配偶承担了更多责任。

sentences.en: So they're becoming more exhausted.
sentences.zh: 所以他们变得更加精疲力竭。

sentences.en: They probably are becoming resentful.
sentences.zh: 他们可能开始产生怨恨。

sentences.en: There's impacts on the children.
sentences.zh: 这对孩子也有影响。

sentences.en: And there's impacts at work.
sentences.zh: 而且在工作中也有影响。

sentences.en: There's not enough research on this particular area, in my opinion.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，关于这一特定领域的研究还不够。

sentences.en: But we do see research on, you know, if a supervisor, for example, is higher in workaholism, they are having negative impacts on their employees,
sentences.zh: 但我们确实看到了一些研究，比如如果一位主管的工作狂倾向较高，他们会对员工产生负面影响，

sentences.en: that their employees are basically feeling like they need to be responding all the time because of this pressure that their boss is putting on them.
sentences.zh: 他们的员工基本上会觉得因为老板施加的压力，他们需要时刻保持响应。

sentences.en: And, you know, just in general, we find workaholism related to negative workplace behaviors like counterproductive work behaviors, which we don't want at work.
sentences.zh: 而且，总的来说，我们发现工作狂与负面的职场行为有关，比如反生产力工作行为，这是我们在工作中不希望看到的。

sentences.en: So things that indirectly or directly harm the organization.
sentences.zh: 所以这些行为会间接或直接地损害组织。

sentences.en: So this could be things like being rude to a coworker or those types of counterproductive work behaviors, not necessarily things like stealing and whatnot.
sentences.zh: 这可能包括对同事粗鲁等反生产力工作行为，不一定是偷窃之类的行为。

sentences.en: But, yeah, we just see universally negative impacts on individuals, those around them, and their work suffers, too.
sentences.zh: 但是，是的，我们看到它对个人及其周围的人产生了普遍的负面影响，工作表现也受到了损害。

sentences.en: We are not finding relationships with job performance, either the self-reported or supervisor-reported performance.
sentences.zh: 我们并没有发现它与工作绩效之间存在关系，无论是自我报告还是主管报告的绩效。

sentences.en: That's consistent across all of our research.
sentences.zh: 这在我们所有的研究中都是一致的。

sentences.en: And we've conducted meta-analyses, which is basically a quantitative synthesis of all the research in this particular area.
sentences.zh: 我们进行了荟萃分析，这基本上是对该领域所有研究的定量综合。

sentences.en: And we're not finding relationships with work performance.
sentences.zh: 我们没有发现它与工作绩效之间的关系。

sentences.en: So workaholic behaviors are not making people better workers, and they're making them more difficult to be around, to be quite honeSt.
sentences.zh: 所以，说实话，工作狂行为并不能让人成为更好的员工，反而让人更难相处。

sentences.en: In my opinion, it's very clear that the impacts are negative.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，很明显这些影响是负面的。

sentences.en: Do workaholics themselves tend to think that by being on all the time that that's going to help their careers, even though the research shows that it doesn't?
sentences.zh: 工作狂自己是否倾向于认为，时刻保持在线有助于他们的职业生涯，尽管研究表明事实并非如此？

sentences.en: I mean, are they deluded?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们是在自欺欺人吗？

sentences.en: Well, for my book, I interviewed many individuals from Workaholics Anonymous.
sentences.zh: 为了写书，我采访了许多来自“工作狂匿名会”的人。

sentences.en: So that's actually a real organization that exists.
sentences.zh: 那确实是一个真实存在的组织。

sentences.en: And so I feel like the answer to your question, it comes from, like, just hearing from self-described workaholics.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这个问题的答案来自于倾听那些自称是工作狂的人的讲述。

sentences.en: And I can say that in many cases, yes, it's almost like they trick themselves into, this is what I have to do.
sentences.zh: 我可以肯定地说，在许多情况下，是的，他们几乎是在欺骗自己，认为这是我必须做的事。

sentences.en: This is what I need, even in the face of negative health consequences.
sentences.zh: 即使面对负面的健康后果，这也是我所需要的。

sentences.en: And I kid you not, every single person I interviewed from Workaholics Anonymous had some sort of health impact of their workaholism.
sentences.zh: 我没骗你，我采访的每一个“工作狂匿名会”的人，他们的工作狂行为都对健康产生了一定影响。

sentences.en: And even with that, you know, I distinctly remember one man I spoke to, he said he will never stop working.
sentences.zh: 即便如此，我清楚地记得我采访过的一位男士，他说他永远不会停止工作。

sentences.en: He will literally work until he dies.
sentences.zh: 他真的会工作到死为止。

sentences.en: And it did not matter that he's had, you know, a heart attack in the past and his wife has said he was, that she was going to divorce him.
sentences.zh: 他过去曾心脏病发作，妻子也曾说要和他离婚，但这对他来说都无所谓。

sentences.en: It didn't matter to him.
sentences.zh: 这对他来说并不重要。

sentences.en: That was, that was what he wanted.
sentences.zh: 那就是他想要的。

sentences.en: And that with him, the only reason he was part of Workaholics Anonymous is his wife said, you're going to do this or I'm leaving you.
sentences.zh: 而对于他来说，他参加“工作狂匿名会”的唯一原因是他妻子说：“你要么去参加，要么我就离开你。”

sentences.en: And so it's almost like he's dragged into this.
sentences.zh: 所以他几乎是被拖进去的。

sentences.en: And I relate personally to, you know, this is why I studied it in the first place is I relate to this idea of kind of telling yourself, I'm doing this for this reason.
sentences.zh: 我个人也能感同身受，这就是我最初研究它的原因，我能理解那种告诉自己“我这样做是有原因的”的想法。

sentences.en: I'm doing this because I need to, you know, this will, this will help me succeed.
sentences.zh: 我这样做是因为我需要，你知道，这会帮助我成功。

sentences.en: So I do think there is a lot of confirming this with yourself.
sentences.zh: 所以我确实认为，这其中有很多自我确认的成分。

sentences.en: Then are there particular jobs where the expectations are so high that workaholism is encouraged, if not expected?
sentences.zh: 那么，是否存在某些工作，其期望值高到即使不被要求，工作狂倾向也会受到鼓励？

sentences.en: I mean, I'm thinking of some law firms where people are just expected to put in crazy hours or even, you know, in here in D.C., people who work on Capitol Hill,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我想到了一些律师事务所，人们被期望投入疯狂的工作时间，甚至在华盛顿特区，在国会山工作的人，

sentences.en: they do crazy hours.
sentences.zh: 他们工作时间非常疯狂。

sentences.en: I mean, you're expected to be there, you know, all night because Congress is in.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，因为国会在开会，你被期望整晚都在那里。

sentences.en: You know, is that the problem that the jobs are encouraging workaholism?
sentences.zh: 你知道，问题在于这些工作在鼓励工作狂吗？

sentences.en: That's part of the problem.
sentences.zh: 这是问题的一部分。

sentences.en: And, you know, there are certainly these types of jobs and occupations that the culture is, it's a workaholic culture.
sentences.zh: 而且，确实存在这些类型的工作和职业，其文化就是一种工作狂文化。

sentences.en: This is what newcomers are told when they get in.
sentences.zh: 这是新人入职时被告知的情况。

sentences.en: Let me give you an example.
sentences.zh: 让我给你举个例子。

sentences.en: One woman I interviewed for the book, she worked at one of the big consulting firMs.
sentences.zh: 我为这本书采访过的一位女士，她在一家大型咨询公司工作。

sentences.en: And the very first day, her co-worker said, look, let me tell you something.
sentences.zh: 第一天，她的同事就对她说：“听着，我告诉你一件事。”

sentences.en: If you ever need to leave to go to a doctor's appointment or something like that, leave your purse on your desk and just take your keys.
sentences.zh: “如果你需要离开去赴约看医生之类的，把包留在桌上，只带钥匙走。”

sentences.en: Hmm, why would that be?
sentences.zh: 嗯，为什么会这样？

sentences.en: Well, I mean, because we know that if we're going to actually leave work to go to an appointment, of course, we're going to take our purse.
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为我们知道，如果我们真的要离开工作去赴约，当然会带上包。

sentences.en: And so it was, you know, basically sending that signal that you don't leave your desk.
sentences.zh: 所以这基本上是在传递一个信号：不要离开你的办公桌。

sentences.en: And, you know, jobs like that, like you said, in D.C., some of the government jobs, I mean, doctors, lawyers, you name it.
sentences.zh: 而且，像这样的工作，正如你所说，在华盛顿特区，一些政府工作，医生、律师，等等。

sentences.en: But what was really fascinating was in my research, you know, I have had people in all sorts of jobs, like across the whole range, K through 12 teachers.
sentences.zh: 但真正令人着迷的是，在我的研究中，我接触过各种各样工作的人，涵盖了整个范围，包括K-12教师。

sentences.en: You know, I even had a race car driver and a llama farmer.
sentences.zh: 我甚至采访过赛车手和美洲驼饲养员。

sentences.en: I mean, it goes the whole range.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，范围非常广。

sentences.en: So it's not linked to specific jobs.
sentences.zh: 所以它并不局限于特定的工作。

sentences.en: Another person I spoke with, she said she thought it was her job.
sentences.zh: 我采访的另一个人说，她以为是工作的问题。

sentences.en: And so she quit and she got a new job and realized she was still doing the same thing, even though that job wasn't as demanding with their organizational culture.
sentences.zh: 于是她辞职换了一份新工作，却发现自己还在做同样的事情，尽管那份工作的组织文化并没有那么苛刻。

sentences.en: And then that's when she realized, oh, this is partially internally driven.
sentences.zh: 那时她才意识到，哦，这部分是内在驱动的。

sentences.en: So the way I see it, there are some internal drivers that, you know, whether it's dispositional tendencies or whatnot, that do play a role for sure.
sentences.zh: 所以在我看来，确实存在一些内在驱动因素，无论是性格倾向还是其他什么，它们肯定发挥了作用。

sentences.en: But the setting, the organizational culture can exacerbate those workaholic tendencies, basically.
sentences.zh: 但环境，即组织文化，基本上可以加剧那些工作狂倾向。

sentences.en: Is it something that is typical of, say, perfectionists?
sentences.zh: 这是完美主义者所特有的吗？

sentences.en: Perfectionists?
sentences.zh: 完美主义者？

sentences.en: Are those the kinds of people who become workaholics?
sentences.zh: 他们是那种容易成为工作狂的人吗？

sentences.en: They're highly related, I will say.
sentences.zh: 我可以肯定地说，它们高度相关。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So there's different kinds of perfectionists, too.
sentences.zh: 所以完美主义者也有不同的类型。

sentences.en: And we see some of the more, I would say, maladaptive qualities of workaholics, such as feeling negative emotions when you're not working or thinking about work all the time.
sentences.zh: 我们看到了一些工作狂更具适应不良的特质，比如在不工作时感到负面情绪，或者一直想着工作。

sentences.en: In my research, those two in particular seem to be related to the aspect of perfectionism that is that you're never going to live up to your standards, your internal standards.
sentences.zh: 在我的研究中，这两个特质似乎与完美主义的一个方面有关，即你永远无法达到你的标准，你的内在标准。

sentences.en: Whereas some people call it the more productive dimension of perfectionism, perfectionistic strivings, which is like perhaps considered the healthier aspect.
sentences.zh: 而有些人称之为完美主义中更具生产力的维度，即“完美主义追求”，这可能被认为是更健康的一面。

sentences.en: That's more related to the behavioral and the motivational components of workaholism.
sentences.zh: 这与工作狂的行为和动机组成部分更为相关。

sentences.en: So the bottom line is they're very highly related.
sentences.zh: 所以底线是它们高度相关。

sentences.en: And we see perfectionistic tendencies in your childhood that are kind of like early indicators.
sentences.zh: 我们在童年时期就能看到完美主义倾向，这算是早期指标。

sentences.en: So, yeah, a lot of workaholics are also perfectionists.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，很多工作狂也是完美主义者。

sentences.en: And just to follow up on that, I mean, if I were a parent of a child and I thought that there was potential workaholism flowering there, I mean, what would I be looking for?
sentences.zh: 顺便问一下，如果我是孩子的家长，觉得孩子身上有工作狂的苗头，我应该注意什么？

sentences.en: There is there's actually a concept called school addiction that I've read about.
sentences.zh: 实际上有一个概念叫“学习成瘾”，我读到过。

sentences.en: I haven't personally studied it.
sentences.zh: 我本人没有研究过它。

sentences.en: But, yeah, you can, I think, look for the same sort of patterns, you know, if your your child is constantly worried about their grade or you see them, you know,
sentences.zh: 但是，是的，我认为你可以寻找同样的模式，你知道，如果你的孩子总是担心他们的成绩，或者你看到他们，你知道，

sentences.en: instead of taking a moment to play with friends, they are studying for their exam, which is two weeks away for hours, you know, and not being able to put their schoolwork down.
sentences.zh: 他们不是花时间去和朋友玩，而是花几个小时准备两周后的考试，你知道，无法放下学业。

sentences.en: I think those are really good indicators that there's some workaholic tendencies developing for sure.
sentences.zh: 我认为这些确实是工作狂倾向正在形成的良好指标。

sentences.en: Well, our country is sometimes stereotyped as a country of workaholics.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们国家有时被刻板印象为工作狂之国。

sentences.en: And I'm wondering if that's borne out in the research.
sentences.zh: 我想知道研究是否证实了这一点。

sentences.en: There are some cross-cultural studies that show that some cultures, you know, on average tend to show higher levels of workaholism.
sentences.zh: 有一些跨文化研究表明，某些文化背景下的人平均而言往往表现出更高水平的工作狂倾向。

sentences.en: U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国

sentences.en: is one of them.
sentences.zh: 就是其中之一。

sentences.en: Japan, China, South Korea.
sentences.zh: 日本、中国、韩国。

sentences.en: Asia, those are probably the ones that show the highest levels.
sentences.zh: 亚洲，这些国家可能表现出最高水平。

sentences.en: What's interesting, though, is Western Europe countries, a lot of them, especially like the Nordic countries, we see lower levels on average, again,
sentences.zh: 但有趣的是，西欧国家，其中很多，尤其是北欧国家，我们再次看到平均水平较低，

sentences.en: but there's not a ton of research on this.
sentences.zh: 但关于这方面的研究并不多。

sentences.en: But if I had to explain where most workaholism researchers are, it's in Europe, which we would think we need more of the research here.
sentences.zh: 但如果我必须解释大多数工作狂研究人员在哪里，那是在欧洲，我们认为那里需要更多的研究。

sentences.en: But that, I think, just goes to show that it's just culturally acceptable here.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这恰恰说明它在那里是文化上可以接受的。

sentences.en: And, you know, maybe that's why in Europe we see more researchers studying this phenomenon because people take it more seriously.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，也许这就是为什么在欧洲我们看到更多的研究人员在研究这种现象，因为人们更认真地对待它。

sentences.en: Well, we don't get a lot of vacation in this country, you know, compared to other places.
sentences.zh: 嗯，与其他地方相比，我们国家的假期并不多，你知道的。

sentences.en: And I'm wondering, is that something that would help mitigate workaholism or help to promote a healthier relationship that workers have with their workplace?
sentences.zh: 我想知道，这是否有助于减轻工作狂倾向，或者有助于促进员工与工作场所之间更健康的关系？

sentences.en: I would love more vacation.
sentences.zh: 我希望能有更多的假期。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But would you take it?
sentences.zh: 但你会休假吗？

sentences.en: Oh, I mean, isn't that the million dollar question?
sentences.zh: 哦，我的意思是，这难道不是那个价值百万美元的问题吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So I do think, you know, as a society, we need more sanctioned vacation days, you know, but regulations that, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以我确实认为，作为一个社会，我们需要更多受认可的假期，你知道，但法规，你知道，

sentences.en: mandate that organizations have to give so much vacation time because we are far short compared to other countries in terms of days off.
sentences.zh: 强制要求组织必须提供这么多假期，因为与其它国家相比，我们的休息日远远不够。

sentences.en: But I do think that even with that, we would need to make sure people take it, you know, use it or lose it policies sometimes are beneficial.
sentences.zh: 但我确实认为，即使有了这些，我们也需要确保人们去休假，你知道，有时“不用就作废”的政策是有益的。

sentences.en: I think people don't want to lose something that they that they have.
sentences.zh: 我认为人们不想失去他们已经拥有的东西。

sentences.en: But things like unlimited vacation time, I don't really think are the solution because then it turns into this weird pressure of like, well, what are my peers taking?
sentences.zh: 但像无限假期这样的事情，我真的不认为这是解决方案，因为那样会变成一种奇怪的压力，比如，我的同事在休多少假？

sentences.en: Like, what are my coworkers taking in terms of days off?
sentences.zh: 比如，我的同事在休息日方面休了多少假？

sentences.en: I don't want to look, you know, like I'm taking too much.
sentences.zh: 我不想看起来，你知道，好像我休得太多了。

sentences.en: Um, and so I definitely think that, you know, having it taken out of the workers control almost and, you know, the organization or some regulations saying, no,
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以我绝对认为，你知道，几乎把决定权从员工手中拿走，你知道，由组织或某些法规说，不，

sentences.en: these are the days you have to take.
sentences.zh: 这些是你必须休的日子。

sentences.en: And, you know, there are even right to disconnect laws in some European countries.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，在一些欧洲国家甚至有“断开连接权”法律。

sentences.en: I don't know if I'm necessarily 100 percent on board with that, but it's an interesting concept.
sentences.zh: 我不知道我是否百分之百赞同这一点，但这是一个有趣的概念。

sentences.en: Right to disconnect laws is basically that the organization is not allowed to reach out to the employee if they are, you know, off the clock.
sentences.zh: “断开连接权”法律基本上是指，如果员工下班了，组织不允许联系他们。

sentences.en: So, again, I don't know if I'm completely on board with that, but the philosophy behind that I am because I do think setting those norms and, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以，再次声明，我不知道我是否完全赞同这一点，但我赞同其背后的理念，因为我确实认为设定这些规范，你知道，

sentences.en: making sure it's not expected and organizations really, really shouldn't unless there's an emergency that can help people to truly disconnect.
sentences.zh: 确保不被期待，除非有紧急情况，否则组织真的、真的不应该联系，这可以帮助人们真正地断开连接。

sentences.en: We're going to take a short break.
sentences.zh: 我们要休息一下。

sentences.en: When we return, we'll talk about the technology that keeps us tethered to our work, even when we're out of the office.
sentences.zh: 回来后，我们将讨论那些即使在我们离开办公室时也将我们与工作紧密相连的技术。

sentences.en: Many of us work from home these days, especially since the pandemic, and we have our work emails on our personal phones and computers so we can check anytime.
sentences.zh: 如今我们许多人都在家工作，特别是在疫情之后，我们的个人手机和电脑上有工作邮件，所以我们可以随时查看。

sentences.en: Has workaholism gotten more common, do you think, as technology has made us more reachable?
sentences.zh: 你认为随着技术使我们更容易被联系到，工作狂倾向变得更普遍了吗？

sentences.en: What we do know from the research is that technology does tether us to work in an unhealthy way and simply just having that access to work 24-7 and them having access to you 24-7,
sentences.zh: 我们从研究中得知，技术确实以一种不健康的方式将我们与工作捆绑在一起，仅仅是拥有全天候接触工作的机会，以及他们全天候接触你的机会，

sentences.en: really what it's hindering is your ability to psychologically detach from work because you're always, you know that you're always possibly reachable.
sentences.zh: 真正阻碍的是你从心理上脱离工作的能力，因为你总是，你知道你总是可能被联系到。

sentences.en: And having that technology is very tempting.
sentences.zh: 拥有这种技术是非常诱人的。

sentences.en: If you have these workaholic tendencies, you're much more likely to have your email go to your phone and check it just throughout the day.
sentences.zh: 如果你有这些工作狂倾向，你更有可能让邮件发送到手机上，并在一天中随时查看。

sentences.en: Just, it almost becomes a habit.
sentences.zh: 这几乎变成了一种习惯。

sentences.en: A lot of us have this, you know, just if we're bored, if we're in line at the grocery store, what do we do?
sentences.zh: 我们很多人都有这种，你知道，如果我们无聊，如果我们在杂货店排队，我们会做什么？

sentences.en: We pull out our phone and maybe check our email.
sentences.zh: 我们会拿出手机，也许查看一下邮件。

sentences.en: Maybe you can relate to that.
sentences.zh: 也许你能感同身受。

sentences.en: Are there other things that workplaces can do to basically discourage people from becoming workaholics or, you know, manifesting those tendencies?
sentences.zh: 工作场所还能做些什么来基本上阻止人们成为工作狂，或者，你知道，表现出这些倾向？

sentences.en: Yeah, there's a ton of things they can do if they're willing to fully, like, see that through.
sentences.zh: 是的，如果他们愿意完全贯彻执行，他们可以做很多事情。

sentences.en: The culture broadly plays a role and then how that manifests with the leader behaviors and what is rewarded is all something to think about.
sentences.zh: 文化在很大程度上起着作用，然后这如何通过领导行为表现出来以及什么受到奖励，都是需要考虑的事情。

sentences.en: So, for example, is the organization rewarding and praising people for being, you know, accessible on the weekends and after hours?
sentences.zh: 例如，组织是否在奖励和表扬那些，你知道，在周末和下班后保持在线的人？

sentences.en: One of the companies I spoke with, one of their employees told me that the CEO in an all-hands call was praising another, you know,
sentences.zh: 我交谈过的公司之一，他们的一名员工告诉我，首席执行官在全员会议上表扬了另一位，你知道，

sentences.en: one of the employees for being available whenever he needed him.
sentences.zh: 其中一名员工，因为他随时都能被找到。

sentences.en: But the issue was he worked all the way around the world.
sentences.zh: 但问题是他是在世界另一端工作的。

sentences.en: And so, you know, being available all the time meant this person was up all night, basically.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，随时都能被找到意味着这个人基本上整晚都没睡。

sentences.en: And so, those are little signals that give indications of what is valued in that culture or in the organizational culture.
sentences.zh: 所以，这些是小信号，表明了那种文化或组织文化中什么是有价值的。

sentences.en: And so, what is rewarded, who is rewarded and why?
sentences.zh: 所以，什么受到奖励，谁受到奖励，以及为什么？

sentences.en: But also things that the leader, I think the leader is, you know, the supervisor, manager is the most direct impact on us, you know.
sentences.zh: 但还有领导者做的事情，我认为领导者，你知道，主管、经理对我们有最直接的影响，你知道。

sentences.en: If our boss is constantly texting us and emailing us and we know that their personality is such that they want a response immediately.
sentences.zh: 如果我们的老板不断地给我们发短信和邮件，我们知道他们的个性是那种想要立即得到回复的人。

sentences.en: A lot of workaholics have this tendency to think everything is urgent.
sentences.zh: 很多工作狂有一种倾向，认为一切都很紧急。

sentences.en: And so, if the manager or the boss has these workaholic tendencies and is constantly pinging their employees and wanting an immediate response,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果经理或老板有这些工作狂倾向，并且不断地给员工发消息并想要立即回复，

sentences.en: that is going to affect the employees negatively, regardless of if they have workaholic tendencies, they're having to jump when the boss says jump.
sentences.zh: 那将对员工产生负面影响，无论他们是否有工作狂倾向，他们都必须在老板说跳的时候跳。

sentences.en: Well, what if you see these tendencies in yourself?
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果你在自己身上看到这些倾向怎么办？

sentences.en: What are some of the things you can do to reduce your workaholism?
sentences.zh: 你可以做些什么来减少你的工作狂倾向？

sentences.en: I mean, you said that that was an issue for you early in your career.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你说过这在你职业生涯早期是一个问题。

sentences.en: So, how do you manage this?
sentences.zh: 那么，你是如何管理这个问题的？

sentences.en: It's a constant battle.
sentences.zh: 这是一场持续的战斗。

sentences.en: I'm not going to lie.
sentences.zh: 我不会撒谎。

sentences.en: I mean, it's not like the tendencies go away, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这些倾向并不会消失，对吧？

sentences.en: So, I think just being really intentional.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为只是要非常刻意地去应对。

sentences.en: And there's a variety of different strategies that I talk about in my book.
sentences.zh: 我在书中谈到了各种不同的策略。

sentences.en: And it's not a one-size-fits-all.
sentences.zh: 而且这不是一种万能的方法。

sentences.en: So, I think it's a matter of trial and error and see what works for you.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为这是一个反复试验的问题，看看什么对你有效。

sentences.en: And I use a combination of things.
sentences.zh: 我使用多种方法的组合。

sentences.en: Because, you know, one strategy is scheduling myself into my daily to-do list, like putting it on my calendar.
sentences.zh: 因为，你知道，一种策略是把我自己的日程安排进每日待办事项清单中，比如把它写在日历上。

sentences.en: Here's the time where I'm going to actually take a lunch break and not be on my computer, but just like relax and eat.
sentences.zh: 这是我真正要休息吃午饭的时间，不使用电脑，只是放松和吃饭。

sentences.en: Or, like, set an alarm on my phone.
sentences.zh: 或者，比如，在手机上设置闹钟。

sentences.en: Okay, now it's time to walk around my building for, you know, 5-10 minutes to just get some fresh air and get away from my desk.
sentences.zh: 好了，现在是时候绕着大楼走一走，你知道，5到10分钟，呼吸一下新鲜空气，离开我的办公桌。

sentences.en: Those little moments of reprieve, like, those are micro breaks.
sentences.zh: 那些短暂的喘息时刻，就像，那些是微休息。

sentences.en: And they can be really helpful in recovery.
sentences.zh: 它们在恢复方面真的很有帮助。

sentences.en: So, another thing that I do, there's a whole literature on recovery strategies that's very related to, you know, the workaholism literature, obviously.
sentences.zh: 所以，我做的另一件事，关于恢复策略有大量的文献，这显然与，你知道，工作狂文献非常相关。

sentences.en: And one recovery strategy from that literature is to engage in what's called a mastery experience.
sentences.zh: 而该文献中的一种恢复策略是参与所谓的“精通体验”。

sentences.en: And I personally love this one.
sentences.zh: 我个人非常喜欢这个。

sentences.en: It works for me because things like relaxation and meditation, I have tried and I have failed.
sentences.zh: 它对我有效，因为像放松和冥想这样的事情，我尝试过，但我失败了。

sentences.en: And I have tried again and I've failed.
sentences.zh: 我又试了一次，我又失败了。

sentences.en: Something about just being idle is very uncomfortable for me.
sentences.zh: 仅仅是无所事事让我感到非常不舒服。

sentences.en: And, you know, I don't love it.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我不喜欢那样。

sentences.en: And so, a mastery experience is a recovery strategy where you're immersing yourself into something not work-related.
sentences.zh: 所以，精通体验是一种恢复策略，你让自己沉浸在与工作无关的事情中。

sentences.en: And it takes your attention and concentration.
sentences.zh: 它需要你的注意力和专注力。

sentences.en: What I love about that is, one, it's been shown to be a very effective recovery strategy.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢它的一点是，第一，它已被证明是一种非常有效的恢复策略。

sentences.en: So, you feel more, you know, engaged the next day at work.
sentences.zh: 所以，你第二天在工作中会感到更，你知道，投入。

sentences.en: You, you, you know, feel more rested.
sentences.zh: 你，你，你知道，感觉更休息好了。

sentences.en: And you're, you're gaining back that energy that you lost, you know, throughout the whole day working.
sentences.zh: 而且你正在找回你失去的能量，你知道，在整天工作之后。

sentences.en: But I'm not sitting there idle.
sentences.zh: 但我不是坐在那里无所事事。

sentences.en: I'm doing something, you know, as long as it's something non-work-related, I am psychologically detaching.
sentences.zh: 我在做某事，你知道，只要是与工作无关的事情，我就在心理上脱离了工作。

sentences.en: Because I'm forcing myself, basically, to think about something else.
sentences.zh: 因为我基本上是在强迫自己去想别的事情。

sentences.en: So, this could be learning a new language.
sentences.zh: 所以，这可以是学习一门新语言。

sentences.en: You know, my editor for the book, he learned, you know, to play.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我的书的编辑，他学会了，你知道，弹奏。

sentences.en: He taught himself how to play guitar, you know.
sentences.zh: 他自学了如何弹吉他，你知道。

sentences.en: So, really, anything that you get joy out of that you can focus on is my favorite recovery strategy for workaholics.
sentences.zh: 所以，真的，任何你从中获得快乐并且可以专注的事情，都是我最喜欢的工作狂恢复策略。

sentences.en: Because it really does seem that a lot of people also struggle with being at reSt.
sentences.zh: 因为它确实看起来很多人在休息时也感到挣扎。

sentences.en: You mentioned Workaholics Anonymous, and I'm wondering, I mean, are they structured the same way that, say, Alcoholics or Narcotics Anonymous are structured?
sentences.zh: 你提到了“工作狂匿名会”，我想知道，我的意思是，它们的结构是否与，比如说，酒精或麻醉品匿名会的结构相同？

sentences.en: Is there 12 steps that you have to go through the same as in those other organizations?
sentences.zh: 是否有12个步骤，你必须像在那些其他组织中一样经历？

sentences.en: Yeah, they are.
sentences.zh: 是的，它们是。

sentences.en: I think it is modeled after, you know, they have the 12 steps, the workbooks, they have sponsors.
sentences.zh: 我认为它是仿照，你知道，他们有12个步骤，工作手册，他们有赞助人。

sentences.en: So, I'm not a member, but, you know, learning about it from my research, it seems very similar to, like, AA, for example.
sentences.zh: 所以，我不是会员，但是，你知道，从我的研究中了解它，它看起来非常类似于，比如，AA（匿名戒酒互助会）。

sentences.en: What are you working on now?
sentences.zh: 你现在在做什么？

sentences.en: I mean, what are the big questions that you're trying to answer?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你正在试图回答哪些大问题？

sentences.en: Well, one of them is looking at these mastery experiences as recovery, you know, and is this actually a more beneficial strategy for people higher in workaholism?
sentences.zh: 嗯，其中之一是研究这些精通体验作为恢复，你知道，这对于工作狂倾向较高的人来说，实际上是一种更有益的策略吗？

sentences.en: And we really don't know enough about that, especially when we think about on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我们对这一点了解得还不够，特别是当我们考虑到日常基础时。

sentences.en: So, how does engaging in a mastery experience at night help you the next day at work?
sentences.zh: 所以，晚上参与精通体验如何帮助你第二天的工作？

sentences.en: Do you, you know, are you more productive?
sentences.zh: 你，你知道，你更有效率了吗？

sentences.en: Are you more engaged?
sentences.zh: 你更投入了吗？

sentences.en: And there's really very little research looking at that particular question.
sentences.zh: 关于那个特定问题，研究确实非常少。

sentences.en: Currently working on updating my meta-analysis, because that is about 10 years old now.
sentences.zh: 目前正在更新我的荟萃分析，因为那已经是大约10年前的事了。

sentences.en: Time goes by faSt.
sentences.zh: 时间过得真快。

sentences.en: So, we're updating that and including all of the studies that have been conducted in, you know, the last 10 years since that was done.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们正在更新它，并包括自那以后，你知道，过去10年里进行的所有研究。

sentences.en: And so, looking to see, are we seeing the same trends in terms of outcomes of workaholism?
sentences.zh: 所以，看看我们是否看到了同样的工作狂结果趋势？

sentences.en: And so, I'm excited about doing that update.
sentences.zh: 所以我对进行那次更新感到兴奋。

sentences.en: So, those are some of my main ones right now.
sentences.zh: 所以，这些是我现在主要关注的一些问题。

sentences.en: But yeah, really looking at day-to-day dynamics, I think, is something that I want to keep diving into.
sentences.zh: 但是是的，真正研究日常动态，我认为是我想要继续深入研究的事情。

sentences.en: And tracing people from day-to-day, like, what are you thinking about when you're not at work?
sentences.zh: 并追踪人们的日常，比如，当你不在工作时你在想什么？

sentences.en: And what is it about your workaholism that you struggle with the most to, like, turn off?
sentences.zh: 关于你的工作狂倾向，你最难做到的是什么，比如，关掉它？

sentences.en: Well, this has been really interesting.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这真的很有趣。

sentences.en: And I think you've given some good ideas to some of our listeners who may have some of these tendencies.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为你为我们的一些听众提供了一些好的想法，他们可能有一些这些倾向。

sentences.en: So, I want to thank you for joining me today, Dr. Clark.
sentences.zh: 所以，我要感谢你今天加入我，克拉克博士。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for having me.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你邀请我。

sentences.en: You can learn more about the psychology of workaholism in the October issue of APA's magazine, Monitor on Psychology.
sentences.zh: 你可以在美国心理学会的杂志《心理学监测》十月刊中了解更多关于工作狂心理学的知识。

sentences.en: It's available for free at www.apa.org forward slash monitor.
sentences.zh: 它可以在 www.apa.org/monitor 免费获取。

sentences.en: You can find previous episodes of Speaking of Psychology on our website at speakingofpsychology.org or on Apple, YouTube, Spotify, or wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 你可以在我们的网站 speakingofpsychology.org 或在 Apple、YouTube、Spotify 或任何你获取播客的地方找到《心理学谈话》之前的剧集。

sentences.en: And if you like what you've heard, please subscribe and leave a review.
sentences.zh: 如果你喜欢你所听到的，请订阅并留下评论。

sentences.en: If you have comments or ideas for future episodes, you can email us at speakingofpsychology at apa.org.
sentences.zh: 如果你对未来的剧集有意见或想法，你可以发送电子邮件至 speakingofpsychology@apa.org。

sentences.en: Speaking of Psychology is produced by Lee Weinerman.
sentences.zh: 《心理学谈话》由李·韦纳曼制作。

sentences.en: Thank you for listening to the American Psychological Association.
sentences.zh: 感谢收听美国心理学会的节目。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。
